_expect.name: Mortal Combat Area/ Light Post Boulders

al_mortal_combat_area_light_post_boulder.blurb: A small bouldering sector inside the Mortal Combat area of Horse Pens 40, the sandstone boulder park in Alabama. Nine problems live here, starting at an easy V1 and topping out with a pair of V7s, though most fall between V2 and V5, so a mixed group can find something. Reports describe the spot as mostly shaded. A big boulder standing near a lamp post marks the place, reached by following the trail that leaves beside the large stage until the woods open up. The park as a whole is known for sloper-heavy problems, and cooler months are named as the best time to visit.

al_the_snail_boulders.blurb: A cluster of nine boulder problems in the Citadel, the sandstone boulderfield near Fort Payne, Alabama. The area is built around a boulder shaped like a snail, whose namesake line is among the field's well-known classics. Grades run from V0 up to V7, with the heaviest concentration at V5, so it leans toward climbers already comfortable on harder problems, though a few easier lines exist. The surrounding Citadel offers featured sandstone with sloper top-outs, roofs and technical slabs, and the boulders sit a short walk from the road and the gravel lot.

al_freebird_buttress.blurb: A small buttress in the Northeast Section of Buck's Pocket, in Jackson County, Alabama. It has nine routes, seven sport and two trad, with a wide spread from 5.9 up to the mid-5.13 range. Three routes sit at 5.9, three at 5.12, and the rest are scattered between, so there is something for moderate and hard sport climbers alike, though not much at the easy end. Reaching it takes a trail walk of roughly twenty minutes from the roadside pull-out for the northern part of the park, and the crag is still lightly documented.

al_creekside.blurb: A fairly large group of boulders beside South Sauty Creek at Buck's Pocket, in northeast Alabama. It has nine problems, all bouldering, and the grades split into two camps: a few easy V0 to V1 lines plus mid-range V4 and V5, then a hard cluster between V8 and V9. The approach is short, five to seven minutes along the main ATV trail with the boulders on your right. The park around it is remote and quiet, tucked into the folds of Sand Mountain, so expect a peaceful session rather than a crowded one.

al_ninja_camp_boulders.blurb: A hard-leaning bouldering area in the Citadel near Fort Payne, Alabama. It has nine problems, none easy: the grades start at V6 and run through V7 and V10 to a single V13 at the top end. It is a fit for sloper enthusiasts, with plenty of sloping holds, and the main line is named as one of the field's test pieces. The boulders lie a few minutes down the trail beyond the Snail, so the walk is short. The sandstone of the wider Citadel brings roofs, sloper top-outs and technical faces.

al_wave_wall.blurb: A compact sport wall in Little River Canyon, Alabama, right beside the Wolf Creek Overlook. Nine bolted lines run from 5.11a to 5.13c, with most between 5.11 and 5.12, so it is a place for strong sport climbers rather than beginners. The routes are full length and finish at the canyon rim, and the climbing is described as clean and enjoyable. The walk is only about a hundred yards, but the descent to the base involves a rappel. The canyon's sandstone is steep, powerful and technical, and climbing is possible through much of the year.
